JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 20-01-2024 at about 8.20 to 8.20 p.m., the petitioner was crossing the road near Shankarapuram, Bull Temple main road, infront of Sri Puttanna Chetty Complex road, with care and caution and by observing the vehicles plying on the road.

At that time, the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418, came from same road i.e. Chamarajapet 5th Main road, from Ramakrishna Aashrama side, in a rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

entities.text: KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident he was bright student in his college.

But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby he could not attend his college from the date of accident and also he could not participate in co-curricular and sports activities as before.
The V.V. Puram Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy vide policy bearing No.0727003123P112584485 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418 and the same was valid as on the date of accident, subject to terms and conditions of the policy and subject to validity of all vehicular documents.

It has contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EB-9418 was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and the above said vehicle did not have valid permit and other vehicle documents as on the date of accident.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation the petitioner.

It has denied the age,
income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner was crossing the road negligently, without observing the traffic rules and regulations.

Further it is contended that, there is inordinate delay in lodging the complaint, which clearly goes to show that, the petitioner colluding with the respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional police has set up and fix the offending vehicle, which was not involved in the alleged accident.

Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1,
as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 20-01-2024 at about 8.20 to 8.21 p.m.,
on Bull Temple main road, in front of Sri Puttanna Chetty Complex road, near Shankarapuram, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EB-9418 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Nagaraj B.N.
as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 20-01-2024 at about 8.20 to 8.20 p.m.,
when the petitioner was crossing the road near Shankarapuram, Bull Temple main road, infront of Sri Puttanna Chetty Complex road, at that time the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-EB-9418, rode the same in rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was bright student Nithin N vs Sarawanmali on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72432318/
3 in his college.

But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby he could not attend his college from the date of accident and also he could not participate in co-curricular and sports activities as before.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P.5 is certified copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.9 is certified copy of MLC intimation, Ex.P.10 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.11 is discharge summary, Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 101), Ex.P.13 is discharge summary, Ex.P.14 are medical bills (total 2), Ex.P.15 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.16 is clinical notes and Ex.P.17 is x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and crossing the road.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.
The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.10,

has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-EB-9418 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, as he was crossing the road negligently, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EB- 9418.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the said contentions.
Even, the respondents No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EB-9418 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the road.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to his negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

Nithin N vs Sarawanmali on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72432318/
4 13.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that,
at the place of accident there were no traffic signal lights or zebra cross marks for crossing the road by the pedestrian and in order to cross the road from the said place, one has to jump the median road divider wall.

This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner was crossing the road from the place were there was no provision for crossing the road for pedestrians and the said negligent act of the petitioner has resulted in accident.

If the petitioner had not attempted to cross the road from the place where there was no provision for the pedestrians to cross the road, the said accident would not have occurred and he would not have sustained injuries.

On the other hand, if the rider of offending motorcycle had been diligent and taken necessary care while riding his vehicle and if he had ridden his motorcycle with moderate speed, he could have avoided the said accident.
Further, the driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and to observe traffic rules and regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.
It is pertinent to note that, admittedly though the petitioner was minor as on the date of accident, he was aged about 17 years and was studying in the college.
A 17 years aged boy and studying in college, is expected to exercise reasonable care and caution while crossing the road.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 20% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch and Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of road, on Bull Temple main road, infront of Sri Puttanna Chetty Complex road, near Shankarapuram, Bengaluru City, due to dashing of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418 to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and crossing the said road from West to East direction.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EB-9418 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-EB-9418.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. No doubt, there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.

He has clearly stated that, immediately after the accident he shifted the petitioner to KIMS Hospital and as he was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in Nithin N vs Sarawanmali on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72432318/
5

sentences.text: lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
16. There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in Ex.P.2 first information statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

17. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 and 13 discharge summaries, Ex.P.16 clinical notes and Ex.P.17 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has suffered post traumatic fracture of shaft of left tibia.

The P.W.2 who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained the above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 20. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 20-01-2024 at about 8.20 to 8.21 p.m., on Bull Temple main road, in front of Sri Puttanna Chetty Complex road, near Shankarapuram, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418.
But, he has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
For the reasons stated supra, this Court is come to conclusion that, there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner to the extent of 20% in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB-9418 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained post traumatic fracture of shaft of left tibia.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
22. Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 13-08-2006.
The accident has taken place on 20-01-2024 at about 8.20 to 8.21 P.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 17 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered post traumatic fracture of shaft of left tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 42% physical disability of left lower limb and 14% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further,
the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 and 13 discharge summaries, Ex.P.16 clinical notes and Ex.P.17 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
But, the P.W.2 has deposed that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after removal of all implants, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 20-01-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 17- 11-2025, which is after lapse of one year and nine months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, fractures are united and implants are in situ, hip joint movement and muscle power are normal and the range of movement will vary after removal of implants.

Further he has clearly stated that,
the petitioner can perform the day to day activities and continue his avocation with some difficulties.
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries caused to him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the Nithin N vs Sarawanmali on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72432318/
7 instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
23. The P.W.1 has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was II PUC Student.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby he could not attend his college and also he could not participate in co-curricular and sports activities as before.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was studying in 2nd year PUC and due to accidental injuries he has not attended his studies and he could not participate in co- curricular activities and sports.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the petitioner was a student and was not having any independent income.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.

24. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 17 years is 18.

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 10/100 X 18 = Rs.3,56,400/-.
25.
Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 103 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12 and 14.

All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.88,273/-
towards medical expenses.

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e., post traumatic fracture of shaft of left tibia.

As per Ex.P.11 and 13 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days, from 20-01-2024 to 27-01-2024 and 11-04-2024 to 12-04-2024, in KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 10 days as in-patient at KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.

31. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 17 years and unfortunately he has sustained post traumatic fracture of shaft of left tibia.
Further, he has suffered permanent physical disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
32. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

As the petitioner is held liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 20%, after deducting the said value from the total compensation amount, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,92,538/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
34. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-53-EB-9418.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the rider of offending vehicle by name Manish S/o Dolaram was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.RJ2220220005666 to drive the said vehicle and it was valid from 22-09-2022 to 22-07-2041.
The policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.0727003123P112584485, in respect of offending motorcycle, was valid from 12-01-2024 to 11-01-2025.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 20-01-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB- 9418 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, as he was crossing the road negligently, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EB- 9418.
This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner was crossing the road from the place were there was no provision for crossing the road for pedestrians and the said negligent act of the petitioner has resulted in accident.
If the petitioner had not attempted to cross the road from the place where there was no provision for the pedestrians to cross the road, the said accident would not have occurred and he would not have sustained injuries.
On the other hand, if the rider of offending motorcycle had been diligent and taken necessary care while riding his vehicle and if he had ridden his motorcycle with moderate speed, he could have avoided the said accident.
Further, the driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and to observe traffic rules and regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.
A 17 years aged boy and studying in college, is expected to exercise reasonable care and caution while crossing the road.
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 20% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.
When the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EB-9418 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-EB-9418.
In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. No doubt, there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, immediately after the accident he shifted the petitioner to KIMS Hospital and as he was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
16. There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in Ex.P.2 first information statement.
18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Further he has clearly stated that,
the petitioner can perform the day to day activities and continue his avocation with some difficulties.
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries caused to him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was studying in 2nd year PUC and due to accidental injuries he has not attended his studies and he could not participate in co- curricular activities and sports.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the petitioner was a student and was not having any independent income.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EB- 9418 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
